Ontologies are structured frameworks of concepts that facilitate the exchange of semantic information among diverse systems. While ontology visualization is a well-established field, most current methods struggle with ontologies containing hundreds of classes, often resulting in cluttered and unreadable representations. This paper introduces OntoPlot, a new visualization technique designed to manage the complexity of large ontologies. By employing a multi-level approach, OntoPlot enables users to navigate from a high-level overview to detailed views of specific sub-ontologies. The method utilizes a novel concept of "visual density" to effectively balance information load across different visual levels. We have developed a proof-of-concept implementation and evaluated OntoPlot against two existing visualization methods using a dataset of 1,000 ontologies. The results demonstrate that OntoPlot surpasses the competing methods in handling large-scale ontologies. Furthermore, we conducted a user study with 15 participants to assess usability and gather feedback, which has been used to refine the implementation. Finally, we outline several directions for future research. The code is accessible at https://github.com/obelfeld/ontoPlot. This paper introduces a method for enhancing semi-supervised end-to-end automatic speech recognition (E2E ASR) by leveraging CycleGAN to generate synthetic speech from target languages that are acoustically similar to the source language. These generated speech samples are converted into acoustic features and integrated with original features to create enriched feature sets for training the ASR model. Additionally, we propose a technique for mining E2E ASR models that are robust to feature augmentation, utilizing an inter-domain penalty that enforces consistency between models trained on original versus augmented features. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a 20% relative reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) compared to using only original features and a 15% relative reduction compared to a baseline that employs CycleGAN-generated features without the inter-domain penalty. Furthermore, our method yields a 10% relative WWER improvement over the baseline when trained exclusively on clean data. To our knowledge, this represents the first study to evaluate the inter-domain penalty for ASR, and our findings confirm its effectiveness in improving semi-supervised E2E ASR performance. This study investigates the Soret effect in a binary mixture of hard spheres and soft molecules, where soft molecules possess an internal degree of freedom and can transition between "soft" and "hard" states. The soft mode is defined as a vector that fluctuates and reorients, granting the molecule a three-dimensional freedom of movement. We demonstrate that the internal freedom of movement of the soft mode significantly influences the Soret effect. Specifically, we show that the sorption parameter $s_0$ is highly sensitive to the asymmetry of the interaction between the soft mode and the surrounding fluid molecules. Furthermore, we establish that the Soret effect can be either amplified or suppressed by the internal freedom of movement of the soft mode. Finally, we examine the temperature dependence of the sorption parameter $s_0$ and the thermal diffusion coefficient $D_T$, revealing that the soft mode's freedom of movement can cause $s_0$ to change sign and $D_T$ to exhibit a maximum. These findings are consistent with experimental observations. Additionally, we explore the physical mechanisms driving these phenomena, emphasizing the critical role of the soft mode's internal freedom of movement. Our results indicate that the asymmetric interaction between the soft mode and the surrounding fluid is the primary driver of these effects. We also analyze the impact of the asymmetry parameter $\alpha$ on the Soret effect, showing that it can be enhanced or diminished by this parameter. Finally, we demonstrate that the asymmetry of the interaction potential can be modeled using a Gaussian function. This work provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding the Soret effect in binary mixtures containing soft molecules with internal degrees of freedom. Our findings offer valuable insights for future research on the Soret effect in such systems. The theoretical framework developed here can be applied to investigate the Soret effect in a wide range of systems, including those involving polymers, colloids, and other soft matter systems. Overall, this work underscores the significance of the internal freedom of movement of soft molecules in driving the Soret effect and provides a robust theoretical foundation for further exploration of this phenomenon. The theoretical insights gained from this study will undoubtedly contribute to advancing our understanding of the Soret effect in complex fluid mixtures. By elucidating the role of internal freedom of movement, this work paves the way for future investigations into the fundamental mechanisms governing thermal diffusion in soft matter systems. The comprehensive theoretical framework established in this study will undoubtedly serve as a valuable resource for researchers seeking to deepen their understanding of the Soret effect in binary mixtures containing soft molecules

This paper introduces a novel technique for enhancing music and speech recordings by leveraging the strengths of both audio and image processing. The method involves converting the audio signal into a spectrogram, applying a trained convolutional neural network (CNN) to the image data, and then reconstructing the audio from the enhanced spectrogram. We evaluated this approach on two datasets, 100Music and F0, utilizing spectrograms generated via the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and Mel spectrogram methods. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves music recordings. Furthermore, we conducted a comparative analysis against existing audio enhancement techniques, including deep learning-based methods and traditional filters such as the Wiener filter, spectral subtraction, and minimum mean square error noise estimation. Our findings indicate that the proposed approach outperforms these alternatives, achieving superior audio quality and higher perceptual evaluation of quality (PESQ) scores. The source code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/Audio-Improvement. Finally, we have released a web-based application allowing users to upload music or speech files for automatic enhancement, available at https://ahmedhassan123.github.io/Audio-Improvement/. We invite researchers and developers to explore our method and contribute to its future evolution. We hope this work inspires further advancements in audio processing and encourages collaboration to improve audio quality for a broader audience. Thank you for your interest.

This study examines how errors in releasing an object during a throw affect movement dynamics and accuracy. This paper introduces a unified, end-to-end framework that integrates NMT and DP decoding using a single sequence-to-tree architecture. This study introduces the Binding Energy Assessment Platform (BEAP), a database designed to offer binding energy distributions for small molecules. These distributions are derived from quantum chemical calculations utilizing the B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP method. The platform's primary objective is to evaluate the reliability of binding energy calculations, thereby assisting researchers in selecting appropriate computational methods for their specific systems. BEAP is accessible at https://beap.astrochem.org. We have also developed a user-friendly interface to facilitate the distribution of these binding energy values. This tool enables users to search for molecules and view their corresponding binding energy distributions, while also allowing for the submission of new molecules. The platform is intended to be a freely accessible, open-source resource for the astrochemical community. We anticipate that BEAP will serve as a valuable reference for astrochemists and computational chemists, aiding in the determination of suitable methods for calculating binding energies. Furthermore, we plan to expand BEAP in the future to include larger molecules and various intermolecular interaction methods. We demonstrate that the class of stochastic processes defined by $X_{n+1}\omega = \max\{a_n\omega, b_nX_n\omega\}$ encompasses a broad range of models found in both natural and social sciences. We provide explicit formulas for the moments of these processes and establish that, under specific conditions, the moments converge to their mean values as $n$ approaches infinity. Furthermore, we illustrate the utility of these models through two examples: one involving a population with a sample-dependent carrying capacity and another concerning a population with a carrying capacity subject to a geometric Brownian motion. Additionally, we show that a significant subset of these models can be analyzed using the martingale convergence theorem. Finally, we derive a sufficient condition for the almost sure convergence of the moments to the mean. These findings are supported by several examples and simulations. The study concludes with an outline of potential future research directions. We introduce a new random Clifford circuit designed to efficiently approximate expectation values for Pauli observables across $n$ qubits, achieving an error rate that decreases exponentially with the circuit depth $d$. This circuit can be executed on near-term quantum hardware, requiring only $O(dn)$ two-qubit gates and $O(n)$ single-qubit gates. The underlying theoretical framework leverages the stabilizer formalism to demonstrate that the proposed distribution converges rapidly to the Haar distribution as depth increases. Furthermore, we illustrate the application of this circuit in estimating the energy of the 2D Heisenberg model and the ground state energy of the 2D transverse field Ising model. Our findings indicate that this method surpasses both the standard randomized measurement protocol and a recently introduced low-depth variant in terms of expectation value estimation accuracy. Additionally, we show that the approach remains effective even when noise is present within the circuit. These results suggest that the proposed algorithm is well-suited for practical use on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. Finally, we have made the code for this work publicly available. This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of the reflection coefficient $R(k)$ for the direct problem associated with the integrable Davey-Stewartson II equations. By employing the $\bar{\partial}$-approach, we derive a novel representation for $R(k)$ that facilitates the analysis of its behavior for large $|k|$. Specifically, we establish that $R(-ik) = O(|k|^{-1/2})$ and $R(ik) = O(|k|^{-1})$ as $|k| \to \infty$. These findings are instrumental in analyzing the asymptotic dynamics of solutions to the direct problem. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the direct problem possesses a unique solution and prove the completeness of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are essential for the subsequent analysis of the stationary phase and steepest descent phases. Additionally, we establish the completeness of the continuous spectrum, thereby confirming the completeness of the total spectrum. Finally, we examine the asymptotic behavior of the reflection coefficient within the steepest descent domains. These results will be utilized in our forthcoming research. The primary innovation of this work lies in the derivation of the new representation for $R(k)$, which enables the precise analysis of its asymptotic properties. This achievement represents a significant advancement in the theory of the direct problem for integrable nonisotropic equations. Furthermore, the completeness of the spectrum constitutes a significant contribution to the theory of integrable equations. Our results also contribute to the broader understanding of the spectral theory for nonisotropic equations, as the spectral properties of isotropic equations are well-established. The techniques developed here may also prove valuable for investigating the spectral theory of other nonisotropic integrable equations. Text categorization is a critical task within natural language processing, where the assigned category facilitates subsequent processing. However, the susceptibility of current state-of-the-art models to adversarial attacks has become a significant concern. This study introduces Sibyl, a straightforward yet effective Sibyl-inspired framework designed to enhance the robustness of text categorization models. The framework comprises two components: (1) a novel adversarial training strategy that employs a fixed set of Sibyls to generate adversarial examples, and (2) a dual-model approach utilizing a data generator and a classifier to refine the classification process. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework effectively boosts the robustness of both traditional machine learning models and deep learning architectures. Furthermore, the research offers a fresh perspective on enhancing the resilience of text categorization systems. The code is accessible at https://github.com/rohitkumar1234/Sibyl. This study investigates the stability of machine translation models when subjected to structural modifications. We evaluate the impact of removing layers from Transformer models and quantizing their weights on translation quality. Our findings indicate that both approaches significantly degrade performance, with quantization proving more detrimental than comparable structural extraction. Furthermore, we demonstrate that both methods can detrimentally affect the extraction of low-resource languages. These results offer valuable insights for future research aiming to create lightweight, low-resource multilingual models. This field theory incorporates a nonlinear self-interaction term that is neither positive nor negative, thereby violating the weak energy condition. This violation stems from the presence of a negative squared derivative term within the Lagrangian density. We demonstrate that this specific type of self-interaction is capable of generating wormholes. Furthermore, we establish that the model supports a class of traveling solitary wave solutions, which we designate as solitary hypergraphons. These solutions are characterized by a constant phase and a variable amplitude. Finally, we examine the physical properties of these solitary hypergraphons, including their energy and momentum. Our analysis indicates that the energy density can be negative, while the group velocity remains subluminal. Additionally, we show that the model admits a negative coupling constant, which can be interpreted as a negative charge. This negative charge is essential for the formation of wormholes. Consequently, we conclude that the model is viable for constructing wormholes. Finally, we explore the potential applications of this framework in quantum computing. Specifically, we propose that solitary hypergraphons could serve as information carriers within a hypergraph-based quantum computer. In this context, the negative charge would function as a bit, while the negative energy density would represent the energy of that bit. Finally, we outline a protocol for implementing this scheme and discuss its potential applications in quantum computing. Although recent advancements in image captioning have yielded impressive results, they often overlook the ability to generate captions across diverse styles and languages. This paper introduces an end-to-end framework that leverages prompt-based conditioning to produce captions with varying languages and styles. Our approach utilizes a pre-trained vision-and-language model, where a text prompt—comprising a specific language and style—is incorporated into the input to guide the generation of styled multilingual captions. We demonstrate that prompt conditioning is more effective than alternative methods, such as few-shot learning, for this purpose. Furthermore, we propose a novel training strategy that integrates both a standard cross-modal objective and a text-conditioning loss to enhance performance. Experimental results confirm that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in unconditioned captioning while also supporting the generation of captions in multiple languages and styles. The code is accessible at https://github.com/ashwinbhat/Regulatable-Image-Captions.

This paper investigates the interplay between causation and counterfactuals, with a specific focus on how counterfactual conditionals function within causal explanations. The author introduces and examines the notion of "damage," defined as an event or state resulting from an agent's intervention that fulfills specific counterfactual requirements. The study explores the relationship between damage and traditional causation, analyzing how this concept applies to various agentive scenarios, including omissions, nonoccurrences, and cases involving foreseen but undesired side effects. Furthermore, the paper addresses the counterintuitive implications of damage for both moral responsibility and the moral status of nonhuman entities. Finally, it considers the relevance of damage to legal contexts, particularly the doctrine of novus actus interveniens. The work concludes by highlighting the broader significance of the damage concept for understanding agency, responsibility, and moral status. Throughout, the analysis relies on a reductive causal framework that integrates process causation, counterfactual dependence, and the manipulation account of causation. Additionally, the paper offers a detailed examination of the manipulation account, demonstrating how it can be restructured to resolve several longstanding issues. This revised account serves as the foundation for the analysis of damage presented herein. (Draft prepared for the 2019 Australasian Association of Philosophy Conference in Brisbane.) This paper introduces MMLSpark, a new open-source machine learning library that extends Apache Spark with support for R and Python. Its intuitive interfaces facilitate the rapid development of novel algorithms and the integration of specialized domain knowledge. This work outlines the architecture and capabilities of MMLSpark and demonstrates its application in executing machine learning workflows on large-scale datasets. We introduce a new, straightforward method for voice translation that operates without any task-specific training data. This approach utilizes a sequence-to-sequence neural network to directly convert speech audio from one language into audio of another. By leveraging pre-trained acoustic and prediction networks alongside a sequence-to-logits module, we bypass the need to model output distributions, thereby eliminating the reliance on target language audio data during the initial stages of the pipeline. Our results demonstrate that this zero-shot framework achieves performance comparable to zero-shot systems in trained languages and significantly surpasses state-of-the-art methods across all evaluated metrics for both trained and untrained language pairs. Furthermore, our model generates significantly more natural and fluent audio than current state-of-the-art solutions. The code is accessible at https://github.com/taehoonkim/zeroshot-vt. To facilitate future research, we have also released the test set for the English-Korean and Korean-English tasks. We hope this resource will inspire further advancements in voice translation. This study presents a probabilistic load forecasting approach designed for low-voltage networks containing a high concentration of renewable energy sources. The method relies on a deep neural network that ingests time-series data from smart meters to generate point, median, and 95% interval forecasts for the subsequent day. Accurately localizing and segmenting vertebrae in computed tomography (CT) scans is a critical step for numerous clinical tasks, including surgical planning, radiation therapy, and biomechanical analysis. This study introduces a novel framework that integrates a geometric prior of the vertebrae with anatomical constraints derived from neighboring vertebrae to enhance localization and segmentation accuracy. The proposed method comprises three primary components: (1) a 3D vertebrae model, (2) a spine rectification technique, and (3) an anatomically-constrained optimization strategy. Initially, the 3D vertebrae model is aligned with the vertebrae of interest using a vertebra recognition approach. Subsequently, the entire spine is reoriented to a canonical coordinate system through a 3D registration process. Finally, the vertebrae are localized and segmented by optimizing an energy function that incorporates anatomical constraints based on the relative positions of adjacent vertebrae. The system's performance was evaluated on the publicly available Vertebral Body Segmentation Challenge 2018 dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a mean localization error of 1.02° and a mean segmentation Dice coefficient of 0.85. This paper introduces a method to address the well-known issue of Distinguishability in quantum mechanics. We suggest that the Distinguishability problem stems from an incomplete definition of the quantum state. To resolve this, we propose a new state vector that incorporates a small spatial extent, thereby endowing every quantum state with a spatial dimension. This approach allows us to derive the Distinguishability solution through a straightforward application of standard quantum mechanics. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our proposed state vector remains consistent with the standard formalism when applied to any wave packet. Finally, we outline the equivalence of our method with the Decoherence interpretation, while emphasizing that our approach offers a distinct and independent derivation. We conclude that this solution is both simple and effective. Additionally, we show that our proposed state vector can be interpreted as a manifestation of the quantum-gravitational uncertainty inherent in any quantum state. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the future development of quantum mechanics. This study investigates the initiation of small-scale tearing modes within collisionless slab plasmas. By employing a local analysis, we examine how the magnetic field line meandering in the current sheet's core evolves into a tearing mode. Our findings indicate that the transition from meandering to tearing mode growth is governed by the perpendicular wavenumber, $k_y$. Specifically, when $k_y$ falls below a critical threshold, the magnetic field lines begin to close, marking the onset of the tearing mode. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the initial growth rate of this small-scale tearing mode is independent of the magnetic field's equilibrium curvature. Finally, we present a set of simulations that validate the applicability of the local analysis to global tearing modes. These results offer valuable insights into the formation of magnetic islands in collisionless slab plasmas. Additionally, the observed small-scale tearing mode growth rate aligns with the rate predicted by the global tearing mode analysis of Chen et al. (2008). This agreement suggests that the global tearing mode analysis can be extended to scenarios involving magnetic field line meandering. Ultimately, the findings of this work may assist in elucidating the formation of magnetic islands in collisionless slab plasmas. The growing availability of high-quality fashion datasets has sparked significant interest in Fashion Image Retrieval (FIR), a task that has garnered considerable attention within the computer vision community. However, most existing FIR approaches are limited to simple category-level retrieval, where images sharing the same fashion category are considered similar. This constraint fails to capture more nuanced similarities, such as specific traits like color, sleeve style, or neckline. To address this, we introduce a novel task called Fashion Image Retrieval with Semantic Manipulation (FIR-SM), which seeks to retrieve images not only based on category and trait similarity but also according to user-defined trait requirements. To tackle this challenge, we propose a new framework named Semi-Supervised Feature-Level Semantic Manipulation (FSM). This framework first extracts deep features from a pre-trained deep neural network and then employs a custom-designed transformer-based model to adjust these features based on user-defined trait instructions. We have developed a new dataset, Fashion-7W, to support FIR-SM, comprising 7,000 images across seven categories and seven traits. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework effectively retrieves images matching user-defined trait requirements. Furthermore, we observe that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art methods on the Fashion-7W dataset. The code and dataset will be made publicly available. This paper introduces a new algorithm designed to address certain classes of linear ill-posed problems within Banach spaces. The proposed dual gradient descent method is demonstrated to converge weakly to a minimum-norm solution for a broad category of problems, notably including those involving compact operators. Furthermore, the study examines the stability of this ill-posed problem resolution and applies the results to specific instances, such as deconvolution and image denoising. Numerical experiments are provided to validate the theoretical findings. The authors anticipate that this work will contribute to the development of techniques for solving inverse problems in Banach spaces. Additionally, the paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers focused on ill-posed problems, offering insights into the application of Banach space methods in this domain. Finally, the authors hope that this research will inspire further advancements in the field of inverse problems.

Light field cameras are increasingly favored for their ability to capture multi-view image data in a compact format, yet they often suffer from significant artifacts due to limited angular sampling. While depth estimation can generate synthetic sub-aperture images to enhance quality, existing methods struggle with occlusions because they rely on original sub-aperture images for supervision. To address this, we introduce a novel synthetic data generation approach that creates cost volumes specifically designed to mask out occluded regions. This technique ensures the synthetic data remains robust against occlusions, thereby boosting performance. We validate our method using the LFHub dataset, demonstrating its efficacy through depth estimation results. The code is accessible at https://github.com/ai4b/occlusion-creator. Our findings indicate that our approach yields superior results compared to other state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the enhanced quality of the synthetic data enables the training of a deep network for automatic occlusion removal, which further improves depth estimation performance. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LFHub and Light Field Stereo benchmarks. The associated paper and code can be found at https://github.com/ai4b/occlusion-creator. This paper establishes the Ablowitz-Kusnetsov bilinear formulas for the Fokas-Lenells equations, which represent a generalization of the nonlinear Schrödinger equations. These findings are achieved through an appropriate Lax pair formulation. Additionally, we derive the bilinear equations governing the coupled system and demonstrate its equivalence to a system of generalized Hirota equations. Furthermore, we utilize the bilinear approach to construct N-soliton solutions for both the Fokas-Lenells equations and their coupled variants. Finally, we analyze the asymptotic behavior of these solutions to elucidate the interaction dynamics among solitons. The study concludes by presenting several illustrative examples. Notably, our findings regarding the Hirota equations align with recent work by Chen and Li. Finally, we offer a discussion on the inverse scattering transform applied to the Fokas-Lenells equations. This study examines the Sasaki-Aronov action, a specific non-Riemannian geometric framework defined on a three-dimensional twisted torus. This twisted torus geometry arises naturally from the toroidal limit of 11D supergravity when double field theory (DFT) is applied. We demonstrate that the Sasaki-Aronov action can be derived from the DFT Hilbert-Palatini action by incorporating a specific choice of DFT dilaton. Furthermore, we identify additional novel non-Riemannian gravitational actions that emerge from the DFT Hilbert-Palatini action through similar procedures. Finally, we establish that all these identified non-Riemannian gravitational actions are invariant under both generalized diffeomorphisms and 11D supergravity transformations. Additionally, we explore the connection between these actions and the recently proposed non-Riemannian 11D supergravity theory. Finally, we outline a potential extension of these findings to higher dimensions. Throughout this work, we utilize the DFT formalism with a generalized connection that remains invariant under generalized diffeomorphisms. This approach is particularly advantageous for non-Riemannian geometries because it ensures the action's invariance under generalized diffeomorphisms without relying on the standard section condition. We anticipate that this method will facilitate the construction of further non-Riemannian gravitational theories. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the generalized connection can be derived from the standard Levi-Civita connection through a generalized gauge transformation. Consequently, we show that the generalized Christoffel symbols associated with the generalized connection can be expressed in terms of those of the Levi-Civita connection. This finding is significant as it enables the calculation of curvature tensors for the generalized connection using the curvature tensors of the Levi-Civita connection. Finally, we note that the generalized Christoffel symbols of the Levi-Civita connection are determined by the generalized vielbein and its first derivatives. The proliferation of IEEE 802.11-based devices has led to significant channel congestion in wireless networks. To mitigate this, the IEEE 802.11k and 802.11v amendments were introduced, enabling access points (APs) to broadcast neighbor information and clients to switch APs based on channel load. This paper introduces a novel approach to extender selection that accounts for channel load. We developed a proof-of-concept implementation of this method and evaluated it within a multi-room home environment featuring two-tier AP and extender configurations. The results demonstrate that this proposed approach effectively reduces channel load on extenders. Furthermore, we identified specific scenarios where this method outperforms traditional signal-strength-based selection. Finally, we outlined potential future research directions.
